name: Japanese asset bubble
capitalInflow: Combined stock and land capital gains were reported as 452% of nominal GDP during the bubble period.
mainTrigger: Rapid asset-price appreciation amid easy credit, financial liberalization and bullish expectations.
mainCause: Credit expansion and reinforced expectations lifted stock and land prices beyond what the cited Bank of Japan analysis could explain through fundamentals alone.
historicalSummary: Bank of Japan research defines 1987–1990 as the emergence and expansion period. Its published account reports a Nikkei 225 peak of ¥38,915 at end-1989, followed by ¥14,309 in August 1992—more than 60% below the peak.
keyLessons: Stable consumer-price inflation can coexist with destabilising asset-price and credit dynamics.
Equity and land markets can amplify each other through collateral and lending channels.

timeline.title: Acceleration
timeline.detail: The Bank of Japan identifies 1987–1990 as the expansion period.

timeline.title: Burst begins
timeline.detail: The cited Bank of Japan account records sharp equity losses in 1990.
